text:
sam: Thinking about setting a steady refactor rhythm for the runtime facade extract. Thoughts on chunk size vs blast radius? Need guidance on rollbacks and SLA concerns.

marta: +1 on tiny slices. prefer per-endpoint adapters — reduces blast radius. canary per-tenant is easier to reason about.

jordan: we should design a fallback proxy so we can route traffic to the old path if the new facade misbehaves. rollback must be trivial.

nina: metrics to watch: p99 latency, error rate, queue depth, and backend tail requeues. add synthetic end-to-end checks.

marta: proposal: 2-week slice iterations. each slice has a spec, contract-tests, canary ramp (1% -> 25% -> 100%), and a kill-switch. keep PRs < 400 LOC.

sam: db migrations are the wildcard. prefer backward-compatible schema and deploy-staggered readers first.

jordan: dual-write is feasible for short windows; otherwise use read-fallback. include data-consistency checks in the pipeline.

nina: coordinate with SRE for capacity and circuit-breakers. set autoscale guardrails for the canary window.

sam: quick design question — sidecar facade vs central proxy? tradeoffs?

marta: sidecar gives per-tenant isolation and easier testing but higher infra footprint. proxy centralizes routing but concentrates risk.

jordan: sidecar complicates deploys (many agents) and observability; proxy simplifies rollout but needs robust canary routing.

sam: ok. I'll draft the RFC with a checklist and runbook. tagging @marta @nina for a fast review.

nina: don't forget the rollback runbook + test harness (incl. chaos tests for degraded infra).

marta: I can pair on the contract-test suite on Tue.

sam: thanks, will ping you both.
